text:
Maya: Heads up: onboarding rk-mini-ptq produced weird metrics. Anchor bench shows NDCG +1.8% but MRR down 2.2%. Canary CTR flat but volatility on tail queries. We did a quick bisect and found token truncation changes in the prod sampler vs eval.
Ravi: What truncation strategy differences?
Maya: Eval harness used left-truncate to max_tokens, prod sampler right-truncates earlier in pipeline due to summary tokenization. That shifts candidate context and can change reranker ties.
Cheng: Tokenization/truncation parity is a persistent footgun. Recommend we add a tokenizer-params checksum to the model artifact and require exact match during canary roll.
Sasha: Another angle: PTQ changed logits slightly which affects tie-breaker that uses tie-breaker-stable-random seed. Combined with truncation changes, top-k shifts.
OpsBot: Canary 2026-03-23T16:45:00Z deployed rk-mini-ptq to shard-1 (20%). No auto-rollback.
Ravi: Suggest tests: 1) run both truncation modes on the same sample and diff ranked lists, 2) run fp16 baseline with right-truncate to see quant-only effect.
Maya: Doing 1) now. Small sample: query "best budget laptop". Left-truncate ranks candidate A top, right-truncate pushes A to 3 due to different context words.
Cheng: I'll push a small change to require tokenizer param parity and add a CI smoke: compare top-5 overlap between left/right for seed sample.
Sasha: Also log tie-breaker seed explicitly in evaluation artifacts.
Maya: Short-term mitigation: enforce left-truncate in prod for this canary and see CTR.
Ravi: If we see improvement, make it part of bring-up checklist.
Maya: Update: after forcing left-truncate in prod canary, CTR improved +0.6% over previous canary baseline. Still investigating MRR gap.
Cheng: Filing onboarding doc update PR with tokenization checksum requirement and truncation parity checks.
Maya: Thanks team, keep dumping candidate diffs and we should close once we have stable parity checks. :sparkles:
